name: Saint Charles Borromeo
history: Nephew of Pope Pius IV and cardinal archbishop of Milan, he led the reform of the Church after the Council of Trent, founding seminaries and visiting every parish of his huge diocese. In the plague of 1576 he stayed in the city to nurse the sick when the governor fled.
meditation: Reform begins at home. Choose one habit to amend this week.
life: Charles was born in 1538 at the castle of Arona on Lake Maggiore. When his uncle became Pope Pius IV in 1559, he made Charles a cardinal at twenty-one, administrator of the archdiocese of Milan and his chief assistant in Rome. Charles helped bring the Council of Trent to its close in 1563 and oversaw the Roman Catechism that followed it. The sudden death of his elder brother turned him to a more serious life; he was ordained priest and bishop and in 1566 went to live in Milan, which had not had a resident archbishop for decades. He held synods, founded seminaries, taught the catechism to children and visited remote Alpine parishes on foot. In 1569 a member of a religious order he was reforming shot at him while he prayed; he was unhurt. Worn out by work and penance, he died in 1584, aged forty-six.
prayerTo: Saint Charles, shepherd of Milan, you spent yourself for the reform of the Church and did not abandon your people in the plague. Pray for bishops and priests, that they may be faithful and fearless, and for me, that I may begin the renewal of the Church with the conversion of my own heart. Amen.
penance: Examine your conscience carefully tonight and make a plan to go to Confession this week. Visit or help someone who is sick, as Charles did in the plague.
prayer: Safeguard Your Church, O Lord, under the continual protection of St. Charles, Your Confessor and Bishop, so that just as his concern for his flock made him glorious, so his intercession may make us ever fervent in loving You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
